title: Artemisia annua L.: a source of novel antimalarial drugs.
decision_rationale: Relevant historical review; use for discovery and pathway context, not as a substitute for primary studies.

title: Antiprotozoal Effect of Artemisia indica Extracts and Essential Oil.
decision_rationale: Reports oil composition, multiple extract preparations, parasite-panel activity, and mammalian cytotoxicity.

title: Biosynthesis of anti-leishmanial natural products in callus cultures of Artemisia scoparia.
evidence_scope: callus chemistry and Leishmania tropica assay
decision_rationale: Reports a bounded callus-extract experiment with GC-MS and promastigote IC50; crude-extract attribution remains unresolved.

title: [Research advances of biosynthesis, in vivo analysis and pharmacokinetics of chemical constituents in Artemisiae Annuae Herba].
decision_rationale: Relevant review context; scope includes many non-terpene constituents and is not an efficacy estimate.

title: Cloning and molecular analysis of two new sesquiterpene cyclases from Artemisia annua L.
evidence_scope: sesquiterpene-cyclase gene family and tissue expression
decision_rationale: Primary molecular study with tissue-specific expression relevant to terpene evolution.

title: Amorpha-4,11-diene synthase: cloning and functional expression of a key enzyme in the biosynthetic pathway of the novel antimalarial drug artemisinin.
decision_rationale: Recombinant enzyme and heterologous expression directly anchor an artemisinin-pathway step.

title: Artemisinin Related Sesquiterpenes and Essential Oil in Artemisia annua During a Vegetation Period in Vietnam.
decision_rationale: Leaf, flower, fruit, stage, and oil measurements directly address tissue and phenology.

title: Sesquiterpene lactones from the endemic Cape Verdean Artemisia gorgonum.
evidence_scope: isolated sesquiterpene lactones and antiplasmodial assay
decision_rationale: Isolation/NMR and purified-compound assay provide compound-level evidence.

title: Secondary metabolic profiling and artemisinin biosynthesis of two genotypes of Artemisia annua.
decision_rationale: Comparative metabolite profiling directly addresses chemotype and developmental variation.

title: Toxic essential oils. Part II: chemical toxicological pharmacological and microbiological profiles of Artemisia annua L. volatiles.
decision_rationale: Reports composition, chemotype clustering, and toxicity; useful for translation boundaries.

title: Comparison of antimalarial activity of Artemisia turanica extract with current drugs in vivo.
evidence_scope: crude extract and Plasmodium berghei mouse assay
decision_rationale: In-vivo antimalarial evidence is relevant but extract chemistry and late-infection limitations must remain explicit.

title: T-DNA insertion alters the terpenoid content composition and bioactivity of transgenic Artemisia annua.
evidence_scope: terpenoid perturbation and antimalarial extract assay
decision_rationale: Links transformation-associated terpenoid changes to crude-extract bioactivity; does not identify a causal terpene.

title: Transcriptome responses involved in artemisinin production in Artemisia annua L. under UV-B radiation.
decision_rationale: Controlled UV-B experiment directly addresses environment-responsive pathway regulation.

title: Chemistry and leishmanicidal activity of the essential oil from Artemisia absinthium from Cuba.
decision_rationale: Matched composition, in-vitro parasite assays, cytotoxicity, and mouse study make this a high-value mixture-level record.

title: Artemisia annua mutant impaired in artemisinin synthesis demonstrates importance of nonenzymatic conversion in terpenoid metabolism.
evidence_scope: genetic perturbation and trichome metabolic flux
decision_rationale: Loss-of-function and isotope-feeding evidence directly test pathway mechanism within A. annua.

title: A phylogenetic road map to antimalarial Artemisia species.
decision_rationale: Connects phylogeny, ethnobotanical records, and artemisinin detection; does not establish abundance or efficacy.

title: Functional genomics and the biosynthesis of artemisinin.
decision_rationale: Relevant review of trichome biology and CYP71AV1 pathway work; primary evidence is retained separately.

title: [Advances in sesquiterpene synthases cyclases of Artemisia annua].
decision_rationale: Relevant review context for A. annua cyclases; not a new comparative orthology result.

title: DMSO triggers the generation of ROS leading to an increase in artemisinin and dihydroartemisinic acid in Artemisia annua shoot cultures.
decision_rationale: Controlled tissue-culture perturbation links ROS treatment to metabolites and differential pathway responses.

title: Reproductive development modulates gene expression and metabolite levels with possible feedback inhibition of artemisinin in Artemisia annua.
decision_rationale: Directly addresses reproductive stage, tissue, pathway transcripts, and metabolite correlations.

title: Dissection of the phytohormonal regulation of trichome formation and biosynthesis of the antimalarial compound artemisinin in Artemisia annua plants.
decision_rationale: Compares chemotypes and hormone treatments with trichome and metabolite measurements.

title: Methyl jasmonate counteracts boron toxicity by preventing oxidative stress and regulating antioxidant enzyme activities and artemisinin biosynthesis in Artemisia annua L.
decision_rationale: Relevant to stress-mediated artemisinin regulation; safety keyword does not imply human safety evidence.

title: The biosynthesis of artemisinin (Qinghaosu) and the phytochemistry of Artemisia annua L. (Qinghao).
evidence_scope: A. annua phytochemistry and pathway context
decision_rationale: Broad review useful for discovery and historical synthesis, not a substitute for primary evidence.

title: Metabolic engineering of artemisinin biosynthesis in Artemisia annua L.
decision_rationale: Relevant review of engineering strategies; engineered outcomes must be separated from wild-type chemistry.

title: β-Cyclodextrins enhance artemisinin production in Artemisia annua suspension cell cultures.
decision_rationale: Controlled culture experiment changes artemisinin production but is not an intact-plant chemotype comparison.

title: Artemisinin biosynthesis enhancement in transgenic Artemisia annua plants by downregulation of the β-caryophyllene synthase gene.
decision_rationale: Perturbation tests carbon allocation between sesquiterpene branches; crude activity attribution is not assumed.

title: Cloning and characterization of trichome-specific promoter of cpr71av1 gene involved in artemisinin biosynthesis in Artemisia annua L.
decision_rationale: Primary promoter and reporter study relevant to tissue-specific pathway control.

title: The effect of roots and media constituents on trichomes and artemisinin production in Artemisia annua L.
decision_rationale: Controlled culture study separates rooting/media effects from transcript and metabolite observations.

title: Transgenic approach to increase artemisinin content in Artemisia annua L.
decision_rationale: Useful engineering context; transgenic yield changes are not natural comparative evolution.

title: The activity of the artemisinic aldehyde Δ11(13) reductase promoter is important for artemisinin yield in different chemotypes of Artemisia annua L.
decision_rationale: Directly compares high- and low-artemisinin chemotypes and branch-point metabolites.

title: Genetic Transformation of Artemisia carvifolia Buch with rol Genes Enhances Artemisinin Accumulation.
decision_rationale: Relevant alternate-species compound detection and engineering; transformed material is not evidence of wild-type pathway equivalence.

title: GLANDULAR TRICHOME-SPECIFIC WRKY 1 promotes artemisinin biosynthesis in Artemisia annua.
decision_rationale: Primary regulatory study connecting a trichome-specific factor to pathway gene expression.

title: Overexpression and Suppression of Artemisia annua 4-Hydroxy-3-Methylbut-2-enyl Diphosphate Reductase 1 Gene (AaHDR1) Differentially Regulate Artemisinin and Terpenoid Biosynthesis.
evidence_scope: MEP-pathway perturbation and broad terpenoid chemistry
decision_rationale: Bidirectional genetic perturbation links precursor supply to multiple terpene classes.

title: Overexpression of a type-I isopentenyl pyrophosphate isomerase of Artemisia annua in the cytosol leads to high arteannuin B production and artemisinin increase.
decision_rationale: Primary enzyme and transgenic study relevant to precursor allocation and pathway products.

title: Biotechnological approaches for artemisinin production in Artemisia.
decision_rationale: Review useful for discovery of engineering studies; not a comparative species or antiparasitic efficacy result.
